nodes.text: There was also another Liber at Thebes, a tyrant renowned for the power of the magic art. When he had taken possession of women's minds with certain drugs and spells, he ordered the frenzied women to commit cruel crimes at his pleasure, so that he might have noble women, captured in mind, as servants both of his lusts and of his crimes. What crimes he committed, and how great a deed he ordered a mother to do against her son, or sisters against a brother, is told every day on the stage by the authors of tragic poetry, so that the wicked cruelty of the criminal tyrant may be born again forever in the minds of the audience through these grim narrations.

Let these lost men tell me now: who is the stronger, he who calls, commands and shuts in, or he who is called, obeys, and, when he has come, is shut into the body of the man who receives him by the power of the one who commands? We give thanks, Porphyry, to your books: you have betrayed to us the substance of your gods; we have learned through you how far your gods are slaves to men who command them. Your Serapis is called by a man, and comes; and when he has come, he is at once shut in on command, and the necessity of speaking is laid on him, perhaps against his will.
